newsitem.title: USA: Scorecard for U.S. Republican Contract with America.
newsitem.headline: Scorecard for U.S. Republican Contract with America.

text.p: Here are the major items in the Republican "Contract with America" and their status as Congress adjourns:
1. Require Congress to follow its own laws -- passed and signed by President Clinton.
2. Require Congress to pay for any programmes it requires states to implement -- passed and signed by President Clinton.

3. Approve a constitutional amendment requiring a balanced budget and give the president authority to veto individual items in appropriation bills, rather than the entire bill -- the balanced budget amendment passed the House but failed in the Senate by one vote; the line-item veto bill was passed and signed by Clinton.
4. Pass crime and anti-terrorism legislation -- passed and signed by Clinton.
5. Pass a welfare reform bill -- passed and signed by Clinton.
6. Permit Americans getting Social Security to earn up to $30,000 a year without losing benefits -- passed and signed by Clinton.
7. Approve a middle class tax cut with a $500-per-child tax credit -- passed by Congress but vetoed by Clinton.

8. Reform product liability laws and make it harder for investors to sue companies -- the product liability bill was passed but vetoed by Clinton; the securities bill was passed and vetoed but the veto was overridden.

9. Develop a national missile defence system -- Congress passed and Clinton signed a bill increasing missile defence spending by $1 billion, but legislation for a full anti-missile system did not pass.
10. Set term limits for members of Congress -- failed in the House in 1995 and in the Senate this April.
